title: Teaching
text:
Earlier teaching
Between 2017 and 2021, I supported undergraduate courses in psychological measurement, multivariate statistics, quantitative research strategies, descriptive and correlational statistics, and the social and political history of Chile and Latin America.



APPROACH


Methods are most useful when students can see the question behind them
I teach quantitative work as a sequence of research decisions: defining a question, understanding the data-generating process, choosing a defensible model, and communicating uncertainty with clarity.




Concept firstBuild intuition before formalism.


Applied practiceLearn by working through real research problems.


Transparent choicesMake assumptions and trade-offs visible.

title: Matías Montero
text:
SOCIOLOGY OF EDUCATION · SOCIAL NETWORK ANALYSIS



I am a DPhil researcher in Education at the University of Oxford, funded by the UK’s Economic and Social Research Council. My work examines how gender, institutional prestige, and social ties shape academic careers and educational trajectories.

title: Matías Montero
text:
Connecting structures, relationships, and outcomes
My research moves across higher education, schools, and classrooms, using longitudinal and relational methods to understand when institutions reproduce inequality - and when they create room for change.

title: Matías Montero
section: Networks and gender disparities across academic careers
text:
Networks and gender disparities across academic careers
My DPhil investigates the formation and persistence of gender disparities in Latin American education research. I model co-authorship and funding networks over time to examine how individual careers and institutional contexts interact.

title: Research
text: I work on collaborative projects that connect substantive questions about inequality with longitudinal, quantitative, and relational methods. The portfolio below highlights current and recent work from my CV.

title: Research
text:
Current research


DPhil research · 2024-present

Networks and gender disparities across academic careers
My doctoral research examines how co-authorship and research-funding networks shape gendered career trajectories among education researchers in Latin America. It brings together research-on-research, organisational context, and longitudinal network modelling.
Role: Doctoral researcher Institution: University of Oxford Supervisors: Alis Oancea and Lars-Erik Malmberg
longitudinal networks gender higher education



2025-present

Choosing schools with a click
Studies how parents and guardians appropriate information about Chile’s School Admission System and how digital information shapes school choice.
Grant: FONDECYT Regular 1250492 Role: Research Assistant · CIAE, Universidad de Chile



2023-present

Gender segregation across knowledge areas
Investigates the background, moderators, and consequences of gender segregation in Chilean academic secondary education.
Grant: FONDECYT Regular 1231930 PI: Lorena Ortega Role: Research Assistant · CIAE, Universidad de Chile
